[01:02] Jordan Rivera: Amanda, can you give us the current procurement timeline and any hard constraints?
[01:10] Amanda Chu: Sure. we're aiming to present to the IT procurement board on the 10th of March. so ideally we want signed agreements and a PO by mid-March. budget's been provisionally approved but final signoff depends on legal clearing the DPA. also, anything that triggers our third-party security review will push timelines, so we want minimal back-and-forth.
[01:35] Jordan Rivera: Understood. Sofia, on the technical side, if you could speak to our Hosted vs Dedicated tradeoffs for them - maybe start with data isolation and SLAs?
[01:45] Sofia Patel: Yeah. so Hosted gives fastest time to value - you get our API, model catalog, streaming responses. we have customer-level isolation logically, but we don't provide a fully customer-managed vpc with hosted. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools, network isolation, and more strict throughput guarantees. for PHI and regulated workloads we'd recommend Dedicated or our Private option.
[02:08] Dr. Leo Martinez: quick q - with Dedicated can we bring our own KMS? we need CMKs for audit.
[02:15] Sofia Patel: Yes, for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed KMS integrations and HSM workflows. you can manage keys via your cloud provider KMS or bring an HSM. note there is some extra setup time - usually a couple weeks for key rotation and connectivity tests.
[02:32] Ravi Iyer: Another security question: DPA requires encryption in transit, at rest, and key separation. also need audit logs for token-level access. does your platform provide token-level audit trails?
[02:45] Sofia Patel: We emit detailed request logs with token counts, model used, route, and request metadata. audit logs can be forwarded to your logging endpoint and we support long retention as an add-on. small caveat: we redact customer prompt content in some hosted paths by default, but for Dedicated/Private we can retain full logs behind your controls.
[03:10] Jordan Rivera: Amanda, does your legal/IT team have specific SLA numbers they must see?
[03:15] Amanda Chu: Our operations team wants 99.9% uptime for the inference endpoints and a P95 latency SLA for small chat-type requests under 200ms if possible; for larger model runs (longer seq) we can tolerate higher latency but we need stated SLOs. also looking for detailed escalation matrix and credits for outages.
[03:40] Sofia Patel: We can commit to SLA targets on Dedicated - 99.9% uptime and P95 latency targets depending on model and instance type. we typically model latencies in our performance profiles; exact numbers depend on the model variant, quantization, and sequence length. we'll propose an SLA table in the MSA appendix with specific model-class buckets.
[04:05] Dr. Leo Martinez: When you say model-class buckets, is that like small/medium/large or actual families like redwood-13b / 70b?
[04:12] Sofia Patel: Both - we tie SLA banding to performance profiles such as 'small-chat' for fast 2-3 token generations, 'contextual' for 1k token context runs, and 'longform' for >2k. we can map those to specific model families.

[04:40] Speaker 1: (crosstalk)
[04:45] Amanda Chu: On the MSA redline - tanya's team flagged the DPA section around data residency and subprocessor lists, can you confirm subprocessors?
[04:55] Jordan Rivera: Yes - we maintain a subprocessors list, and we'll share the current one with the DPA. we can add a clause for 30 days notice before adding high-risk subprocessors; legal prefers 60 though.
[05:10] Tanya Lopez: 60 days is our standard. also we need to confirm breach notification timelines and whether Redwood will sign contractual liability caps.
[05:20] Jordan Rivera: breach notification is typically 72 hours for material incidents. liability caps are negotiable - we're used to a mutual cap tied to subscription fees, but open to discuss specifics for enterprise deals.
[05:35] Ravi Iyer: on incident response - will you provide post-incident reports and root cause analysis as part of the SLA?
[05:42] Sofia Patel: yes, post-mortem and RCA are included for major incidents; the level of detail can be covered in the incident response appendix.

[06:00] Jordan Rivera: Let's talk pricing for a minute - Amanda you mentioned 250k monthly token volume for the pilot estimate?
[06:07] Amanda Chu: yes that's a ballpark for the first month of pilot with about 3k daily active users hitting the assistant.
[06:12] Jordan Rivera: For that scale we offered two paths: Hosted volume-based pricing or Dedicated reserved capacity. Hosted is simpler with per-token unit pricing and no setup fee. Dedicated is a reserved monthly commit with lower per-token unit economics and an onboarding/setup fee. Sofia, any note on cost delta?
[06:30] Sofia Patel: ballpark - Dedicated lowers per-token unit by ~30-50% depending on model mix; but upfront reservation and config is required. Also Dedicated enables stricter SLOs and isolation.
[06:42] Amanda Chu: Procurement will need a clear TCO calc. can you provide a sample worksheet showing break-even at what volume Dedicated becomes cheaper?
[06:50] Jordan Rivera: Absolutely, we'll include a break-even spreadsheet with assumptions by model class and expected throughput. I'll attach to the MSA deliverable.

[07:10] Dr. Leo Martinez: On the technical benchmark - we would like to run our test prompts and measure P50/P95 on both hosted and dedicated. what data sharing or obfuscation options do we have?
[07:22] Sofia Patel: You can share a synthetic or redacted test set. we can also run the tests in your VPC for Dedicated or in a private test project for Hosted with obfuscated inputs. we recommend running in Dedicated for most accurate SLA comparisons.
[07:40] Ravi Iyer: For DPA, we need contract language on deletion of data on termination and the ability to export logs for audit. can you commit to data deletion windows?
[07:51] Jordan Rivera: Standard is deletion within 30 days of contract termination; for Dedicated/Private we can do expedited deletion and provide attestation. we'll propose options in the DPA.

[08:10] Amanda Chu: On the MSA redline we also had a question about indemnity and any government data exceptions - Polaris handles some government-funded research, so we need clarity there.
[08:22] Tanya Lopez: yes, certain datasets might be restricted, and we need a carve-out that Redwood will not use those for model training and that those are treated as customer confidential.
[08:32] Sofia Patel: We have a clause that customer-provided data is not used to train public models unless opt-in; we can add explicit language for government-funded datasets.

[08:50] Jordan Rivera: Competitors were mentioned - Amanda, you had evaluated OpenAI and Anthropic. what were the runbooks?
[08:58] Amanda Chu: we did quick PoCs - OpenAI had better latency for smaller chat but pricing was a concern at scale; Anthropic's safety features were strong. we liked Redwood for the enterprise SLAs and the Dedicated offering. procurement favors pricing predictability.

[09:18] Sofia Patel: One note - if you require HIPAA-level handling, our Private deployment or Dedicated with BAA addendum is the recommended path. Hosted can be configured but it's less common for PHI.
[09:30] Dr. Leo Martinez: We will need a BAA. is that a separate addendum to the MSA?
[09:36] Jordan Rivera: Yes, BAA is an addendum - we have a standard BAA that can be attached. we'll include that in the packet.

[10:00] [10:00 mark - demo of MSA redline status by Jordan]

[10:20] Tanya Lopez: We need that exact wording, and an audit clause to verify.
[10:24] Jordan Rivera: We'll add the specific line and an audit right clause with reasonable notice windows.

[10:40] [10:40] Ravi Iyer: On network transport - are there IP allowlist options and dedicated peering?
[10:46] Sofia Patel: For Dedicated we support VPC peering and IP allowlists; for Private we do full network integration.

[11:05] Amanda Chu: For procurement signoff we also need a 3-year indemnity clause length question - how do you normally handle indemnity term length?
[11:12] Jordan Rivera: We typically have indemnity provisions aligned to the MSA but the time windows can be negotiated; many customers ask for a 1-3 year lookback for claims.

[11:30] Dr. Leo Martinez: a couple technical specifics - does Redwood support model quantization profiles and can you guarantee behavior across quantized variants? we are concerned about regression impact.
[11:40] Sofia Patel: Yes, we support quantization profiles and have a Redwood Optimize toolkit that recommends quantization by workload. regressions are tracked via our eval hooks and we can include regression monitoring as an add-on.

[14:18] Jordan Rivera: Enterprise support add-on includes 24/7 pager and a dedicated technical account manager. we'll detail escalation matrix and contact points in the SLA appendix.

[14:38] Amanda Chu: procurement needs a line item for onboarding fees and any minimum commitment. what's typical?
[14:45] Jordan Rivera: Onboarding fees vary - for Dedicated there's a setup fee (one-time) depending on infra complexity, usually $10k- $30k. Minimum monthly commit depends on GPU reservations - we'll put examples in the pricing sheet.
